This page lists what changed recently and leaves out what the workshop already teaches. Each item
says what changed, when, where we read it (*Verified (date)* means we opened that page on that
date; *Not read* means we could not and says what we relied on instead) and which module it
touches. Figures a company reports about itself are marked as the company's own. Last reviewed
2026-10-16; the [references](references.qmd#how-checked) page explains how we check sources.
:::

## Measurement {#measurement}

**Google's Meridian is open to everyone.** Google released Meridian, its open-source Bayesian
marketing mix model, to all advertisers on 2025-01-29, after a limited-access period. It works on
geo-level data, models reach and frequency rather than impressions alone, and takes the results of
incrementality experiments as priors, which is the calibration idea of Module 9. Releases have
continued; version 2.1.0 reached PyPI on 2026-09-25 (Apache-2.0). *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[Google's announcement](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/meridian-marketing-mix-model-open-to-everyone/)
("Meridian accounts for reach and frequency, not just impressions"; "easily integrates
incrementality experiment results as priors") and the [repository](https://github.com/google/meridian).
*In this workshop:* Modules 8 to 10 and 17 use PyMC-Marketing; Meridian is the second
open-source Bayesian MMM a team can compare it with. It is not used in a lab because it conflicts
with PyMC-Marketing's pins and prefers a GPU ([decisions](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/DECISIONS.md)).

**Chrome keeps third-party cookies, and most of the Privacy Sandbox is gone.** On 2025-04-22 Google
dropped its plan for a standalone cookie prompt in Chrome and kept the existing settings-based
choice. On 2025-10-17 it retired most Privacy Sandbox technologies, citing low adoption, among them
Topics, Protected Audience and the Attribution Reporting API; CHIPS, FedCM and Private State Tokens
stay. Cookie-based tracking in Chrome therefore lasts longer than teams planned for in 2024, and
the sandbox's privacy-preserving attribution path is no longer coming. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[Next steps for Privacy Sandbox](https://privacysandbox.google.com/blog/privacy-sandbox-next-steps)
("will not be rolling out a new standalone prompt for third-party cookies") and
[Update on plans for Privacy Sandbox technologies](https://privacysandbox.google.com/blog/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies)
("in light of their low levels of adoption, we've decided to retire the following Privacy Sandbox
technologies"). *In this workshop:* Modules 6, 7 and 16: user-level paths remain available in
Chrome for now, and Module 16 shows why they still do not measure incrementality.

**The platforms now sell modeled incrementality.** Meta's "Incremental Attribution" setting steers
delivery toward conversions its models judge incremental, trained on its own conversion-lift
studies; on 2026-01-28 Meta said its Q4 2025 model drove 24% more incremental conversions than
standard attribution and that the product reached a multi-billion-dollar annual run rate seven
months after launch (Meta's own figures). Google's user-based Conversion Lift help page now lists
Search and Performance Max campaigns alongside Display, Video, Demand Gen and App, with a floor of
1,000 observed conversions and a $5,000 minimum budget, and still says to contact a Google
representative. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[Meta newsroom, 2026-01-28](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/01/2026-ai-drives-performance/) ("a 24%
increase in incremental conversions compared to our standard attribution model");
[Google Ads help: set up Conversion Lift based on users](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12005564?hl=en)
("at least 1,000 observed conversions"; "To use Conversion Lift, contact your Google account
representative"). *Not read:* Meta's help page on Incremental Attribution (the page did not open),
so the launch month is not verified. *In this workshop:* Modules 6, 7 and 9. A platform's lift
number is an experiment the platform ran on its own objective; the geo tests of Module 7 are the
independent check.

**Marketers say they will spend more on MMM.** A TransUnion and EMARKETER survey of 196 US marketing
professionals (fielded July 2025, published 2025-10-21) found 47% planning to increase spend on
marketing mix modeling in the next year and confidence in measurement flat. It is a vendor survey
with a paywalled methods chart; take it as directional. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[TransUnion press release](https://newsroom.transunion.com/new-transunion-research-reveals-marketers-confidence-in-measurement-has-stalled/).
*In this workshop:* Day 4.

## Platforms automate the campaign {#platforms}

**Meta's ad delivery runs on retrieval and ranking models that learn from everything.** Meta rebuilt
ad retrieval (Andromeda, announced 2024-12-02) and ranking around one large foundation model, GEM,
built "on an LLM-inspired paradigm". On its Q3 2025 earnings call Meta said combining retrieval and
early-stage ranking raised ads quality 14% on Facebook surfaces, that revenue through its end-to-end
automated Advantage+ products reached a $60 billion annual run rate, and that advertisers using its
video-generation tools rose 20% quarter on quarter; its 2026-10-13 engineering post claims an 18.9%
conversion improvement from GEM since. All figures are Meta's own. The practical change for an
advertiser is where the levers are: targeting is automated, so the inputs that remain are creative
variety, the conversion signal fed back, and independent measurement. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[Andromeda](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/),
[GEM](https://engineering.fb.com/2025/11/10/ml-applications/metas-generative-ads-model-gem-the-central-brain-accelerating-ads-recommendation-ai-innovation/),
[GEM in 2026](https://engineering.fb.com/2026/10/13/ml-applications/metas-generative-ads-model-gem-scaling-the-central-model-and-compute-engine-for-frontier-ads-ai/)
and the [Q3 2025 earnings call transcript](https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/META-Q3-2025-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf).
No research paper on GEM was found; do not cite one. *In this workshop:* Modules 8, 9 and 11: when
the platform optimizes delivery, the ROAS it reports is a model of its own targeting, and a lift
test or an MMM calibrated by one is what tells you what the spend caused.

## New channels: agents and answer engines {#agents}

**AI agents can now shop and pay.** Three open protocols appeared within four months. Google's Agent
Payments Protocol (AP2, 2025-09-16) carries cryptographically signed "mandates" that record what a
user authorized. OpenAI and Stripe's Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP, 2025-09-29, Apache-2.0) powered
Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, first with Etsy sellers; on 2026-03-24 OpenAI pulled Instant Checkout
back as a standalone feature, letting merchants use their own checkout while ChatGPT focuses on
discovery, and the protocol continues. Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, 2026-01-11), built
with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target and Walmart, powers checkout in AI Mode and Gemini. Shopify's
Agentic Storefronts (2025-12-10) sell through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot and report
orders with the originating AI channel; Mastercard (Agent Pay, 2025-04-29) and Visa (Intelligent
Commerce, 2025-04-30) issue agent-specific tokenized credentials with user-set limits. *Verified
(2026-10-16):* [Stripe newsroom](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-openai-instant-checkout),
[Stripe on ACP](https://stripe.com/blog/developing-an-open-standard-for-agentic-commerce),
[Google Cloud on AP2](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-agents-to-payments-ap2-protocol),
[Google on UCP](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/agentic-commerce-ai-tools-protocol-retailers-platforms/),
[Shopify, 2025-12-10](https://www.shopify.com/news/winter-26-edition-agentic-storefronts) and
[2026-03-24](https://www.shopify.com/news/agentic-commerce-momentum),
[Mastercard](https://newsroom.mastercard.com/news/press/2025/april/mastercard-unveils-agent-pay-pioneering-agentic-payments-technology-to-power-commerce-in-the-age-of-ai),
[Visa](https://usa.visa.com/about-visa/newsroom/press-releases.releaseId.21361.html). *Not read:*
OpenAI's own announcement pages (they refused the request); we relied on Stripe as co-announcer and
on [TechCrunch, 2026-03-24](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/24/openais-plans-to-make-chatgpt-more-like-amazon-arent-going-so-well/)
quoting OpenAI for the pull-back. *In this workshop:* Modules 1 to 5 and 16. An agent-referred
order is a new acquisition channel with its own repeat behavior, and a "visit" that is an agent call
breaks the journey data attribution relies on. Treat it as a channel to measure with Modules 2
to 5, not as a touch.

**Answer engines change what "organic" means.** Google rolled AI Mode out to all US users on
2025-05-20, put ads in AI Overviews on desktop and in AI Mode from 2025-05-21, and by 2026-06-03
reported AI Overviews above 2.5 billion monthly users and AI Mode past 1 billion. Pew's panel study
of March 2025 browsing (900 US adults) found users clicked a traditional result on 8% of visits that
showed an AI summary against 15% without one, clicked a source inside the summary on 1% of visits,
and ended the session more often (26% against 16%); Pew reports the association, not a cause.
Adobe's own analytics put AI-referred traffic to US retail sites up 693% year on year over the 2025
holiday season (vendor data). *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[Google, 2025-05-20](https://blog.google/products/search/google-search-ai-mode-update/),
[Google Marketing Live 2025](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/google-marketing-live-2025/),
[Alphabet investor presentation, June 2026](https://blog.google/alphabet/investor-presentation-june-2026/),
[Pew Research, 2025-07-22](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/),
[Adobe, 2026-01-07](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/01/adobe-holiday-shopping-season).
*In this workshop:* Modules 8 and 17. The organic baseline of a marketing mix model fitted across
2025 has a structural break in it; Module 17's residual check is the tool that finds it.

**Retail media keeps compounding.** Amazon's advertising services revenue was $17.7 billion in Q3
2025, up 24% on the year, from its own filing. Retail media networks sell closed-loop measurement on
first-party purchase data: convenient, but attribution inside a walled garden, not incrementality.
*Verified (2026-10-16):* [Amazon Q3 2025 results, SEC exhibit 99.1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000121/amzn-20250930xex991.htm).
*In this workshop:* Modules 8, 10 and 16.

## Notifications under the operating system's control {#notifications}

**The phone can rewrite or silence your push.** iOS 18.1 (October 2024) introduced Apple Intelligence
notification summaries, which condense a stack of notifications into one line. In iOS 18.3 (January
2025) Apple made summaries "temporarily unavailable" for News and Entertainment apps after misleading
summaries of news alerts, set summarized notifications in italics, and added Lock Screen controls to
turn summaries off per app; the press reported their return for news apps with a warning in the iOS
26 betas (2025-07-22). On Android 13 and later an app's notifications are off until it wins the
POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission. The copy a growth team writes may be rewritten before the user
sees it, and the user can mute the app in two taps. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[About iOS 18 updates](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121161) ("Notification summaries for News &
Entertainment apps are temporarily unavailable"; "Easily manage settings for notification summaries
from the Lock Screen"), [Android notification runtime permission](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/notification-permission)
("your app's notifications are off by default"). *Not read:* an Apple page confirming the iOS 26
return; [9to5Mac, 2025-07-22](https://9to5mac.com/2025/07/22/ios-26-beta-4-re-enables-apple-intelligence-notification-summaries-for-news-apps/)
is the evidence. A widely reported Android "notification cooldown" is not on the Android 15 or 16
developer pages we read. *In this workshop:* [Module 18](modules/18-notifications.qmd): the
opt-out is the binding constraint of the volume trade-off, and the operating system makes it cheaper
every year.

## Methods and tools {#methods}

**Sequence models for notification policy.** LinkedIn researchers reframed the send decision as
sequence modeling with a Decision Transformer instead of value-based offline reinforcement learning,
with a multi-reward design for a task that never ends and quantile regression for the return target;
in production it gave +0.72% sessions over a multi-objective conservative-Q-learning agent. A
preprint, not peer reviewed. *Verified (2026-10-16):* [arXiv 2509.02458](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02458)
(submitted 2025-09-02). *In this workshop:* Module 18 fits the value-iteration policy that this
line of work starts from, and its briefing lists the LinkedIn papers it builds on.

**Digital twins of respondents.** Toubia and colleagues at Columbia released Twin-2K-500, a public
dataset of 2,058 US respondents answering more than 500 questions over four waves, to test whether
large-language-model "digital twins" can stand in for people in pretests; the authors report that
twins capture relative differences between people but predict individuals poorly. *Verified
(2026-10-16):* [arXiv 2505.17479](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17479) and the
[authors' project page](https://daplab.cs.columbia.edu/projects/digitaltwins/) (the journal record
in Marketing Science could not be opened). *In this workshop:* Module 6. A simulated respondent can
order message variants before a test; it does not replace the test.

**Open-source tooling moved under us.** PyMC-Marketing reached 1.0.0 on 2026-08-07 ("After two years
of 0.x releases, this is our stable API"), made the multidimensional MMM the default, and in 1.1.0
and 1.2.0 (2026-09-29, the version this workshop pins) restructured the budget optimizer and added a
lift-test case study. CausalPy shipped Bayesian synthetic difference-in-differences in 0.9.0
(2026-07-28) and a 1.0.0 release candidate with geo-lift analysis for MMM calibration (2026-10-06).
Meta's Robyn has had no commit on its main branch since 2025-06-27; the repository is not archived
and carries no deprecation notice, and reports that Meta is winding it down rest on anonymous
sources. *Verified (2026-10-16):* [PyMC-Marketing releases](https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/releases),
[CausalPy releases](https://github.com/pymc-labs/CausalPy/releases),
[Robyn](https://github.com/facebookexperimental/Robyn). *In this workshop:* Modules 7 to 10 and 17;
the package pins are in `_variables.yml` and the [versions page](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/environment/VERSIONS.md).

## Rules {#rules}

**The EU AI Act applies, with its high-risk rules delayed.** Prohibitions and AI-literacy duties
applied from 2025-02-02, obligations for general-purpose AI models from 2025-08-02, and the Act
became generally applicable on 2026-08-02; the "Digital Omnibus on AI", in force since 2026-07-27,
moved the high-risk obligations for Annex III use cases to 2027-12-02 and for product-embedded
systems to 2028-08-02. In the United States, 19 states had comprehensive privacy laws by
2025-10-27, several giving consumers a right to opt out of profiling for automated decisions. France's
competition authority fined Apple €150 million on 2025-03-31 over how App Tracking Transparency was
implemented, without ordering changes to it. *Verified (2026-10-16):*
[European Commission, regulatory framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
(updated 2026-08-03), [IAPP state privacy overview](https://iapp.org/resources/article/us-state-privacy-laws-overview/)
("each of the 19 states that have passed comprehensive privacy laws to date"),
[Autorité de la concurrence](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/targeted-advertising-autorite-de-la-concurrence-imposes-fine-eu150000000-apple).
*Not read:* the Official Journal text of the omnibus regulation and the per-state effective dates
(member-gated pages). *In this workshop:* Modules 11, 15 and 18, which make automated decisions
about individuals: whom to discount, whom to credit, whom to notify. Keep the opt-out and the
explanation of the rule as part of the deliverable.

## What we checked and left out {#left-out}

Claims we could not trace to a primary or reputable source are not on this page: that Meta will
offer fully AI-generated ads by the end of 2026; a Meta research paper on GEM; an Android
"notification cooldown"; Shopify's "11x" growth in AI-attributed orders; an incrementality-adoption
percentage from the EMARKETER survey (paywalled); and that Meta is winding down Robyn. If you have a
primary source for any of them, [open an issue](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/issues).
